title: Julius Caesar
author: James Baldwin
summary: 恺撒宁可做一村之首也不做罗马第二，并在风暴中显出镇定。
publicDomainBasis: Published 1896 by the American Book Company; author James Baldwin (1841–1925). Public domain in the United States and in China (author's life plus 70 years).

paragraphs.en: Nearly two thousand years ago there lived in Rome a man whose name was Julius Caesar. He was the greatest of all the Romans.
paragraphs.zh: 将近两千年前，罗马住着一个名叫尤利乌斯·恺撒的人。他是所有罗马人中最伟大的一位。

paragraphs.en: He was a brave warrior, and had conquered many countries for Rome. He was wise in planning and in doing. He knew how to make men both love and fear him.
paragraphs.zh: 他是一位勇敢的战士，为罗马征服了许多国家。他善于谋划，也善于行动。他懂得如何让人既爱他又敬畏他。

paragraphs.en: At last he made himself the ruler of Rome. Some said that he wished to become its king. But the Romans at that time did not believe in kings.
paragraphs.zh: 最后，他让自己成了罗马的统治者。有人说他想当国王，但当时的罗马人并不接受国王。

paragraphs.en: Once when Cae-sar was passing through a little country village, all the men, women, and children of the place came out to see him. There were not more than fifty of them, all together, and they were led by their mayor, who told each one what to do.
paragraphs.zh: 有一次，恺撒路过一个小村庄，村里的男女老少都出来看他。他们总共不超过五十人，由村长带领，村长指挥着每个人该站哪里、该做什么。

paragraphs.en: These simple people stood by the roadside and watched Caesar pass. The mayor looked very proud and happy; for was he not the ruler of this village? He felt that he was almost as great a man as Caesar himself.
paragraphs.zh: 这些淳朴的人站在路边，看着恺撒经过。村长显得非常自豪、非常快乐，因为他不就是这个村子的统治者吗？他觉得自己几乎和恺撒本人一样伟大。

paragraphs.en: Some of the fine officers who were with Caesar laughed. They said, "See how that fellow struts at the head of his little flock!"
paragraphs.zh: 恺撒身边一些衣着考究的军官笑了起来。他们说：“瞧那家伙，领着他那一小群羊，走得多神气！”

paragraphs.en: "Laugh as you will," said Caesar, "he has reason to be proud. I would rather be the head man of a village than the second man in Rome!"
paragraphs.zh: “你们尽管笑吧，”恺撒说，“他有权感到自豪。我宁愿做一个村子的头领，也不愿做罗马的第二号人物！”

paragraphs.en: At another time, Caesar was crossing a narrow sea in a boat. Before he was halfway to the farther shore, a storm overtook him. The wind blew hard; the waves dashed high; the lightning flashed; the thunder rolled.
paragraphs.zh: 还有一次，恺撒乘船横渡一片狭窄的海域。还没走到对岸的一半，风暴就袭来了。狂风大作，浪涛高涌，电光闪闪，雷声隆隆。

paragraphs.en: It seemed every minute as though the boat would sink. The captain was in great fright. He had crossed the sea many times, but never in such a storm as this. He trembled with fear; he could not guide the boat; he fell down upon his knees; he moaned, "All is lost! all is lost!"
paragraphs.zh: 每一刻都让人觉得船要沉了。船长吓得魂飞魄散。他多次渡过这片海，却从未遇上这样的风暴。他害怕得发抖，无法掌舵，跪倒在船上，呻吟道：“全完了！全完了！”

paragraphs.en: But Caesar was not afraid. He bade the man get up and take his oars again.
paragraphs.zh: 但恺撒并不害怕。他命令船长站起来，重新拿起船桨。

paragraphs.en: "Why should you be afraid?" he said. "The boat will not be lost; for you have Caesar on board."
paragraphs.zh: “你为什么要害怕？”他说，“船不会沉，因为有恺撒在船上。”
